image-alt-not-descriptive: WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Understanding: a text alternative serves the equivalent purpose); ACT rule 'Image accessible name is descriptive'. Descriptive means the name conveys the image's content, or for an image inside a link or button, its function. Violation: the name describes something else, is a file name or placeholder, or contradicts the image or its function; an image that is the only content of a link or button and whose name describes its appearance instead of the action (e.g. 'inkjet printer' on a Print button); an informative image that carries text or data (a chart, diagram, map, organisation chart, flowchart, table, price comparison, certificate) whose name only identifies the image or its subject (e.g. 'network map', 'organisation chart', 'loan decision flowchart'), when that information is not given in text on the page or in a programmatically associated description. Not a violation: a brief but accurate name; an image inside a link or button that has its own visible text naming the action, when the image's name identifies the image (e.g. 'Google logo' in a 'Sign up with Google' button): redundant at most; a name of a chart or diagram that states its main point or trend, even if it omits individual values; a name that repeats adjacent text; a complex image whose information is given in nearby text or an associated description. A plain or empty area where an should be can mean that the image did not load when the state was recorded; that alone is not evidence against the name; but an element with role img that is not an (e.g. a div drawn with CSS) or a visible placeholder graphic (e.g. a box reading 'Product photo') is what the page shows: a name describing a specific picture that is not shown does not describe it; then judge the name against the image's file name or source URL, the link or button it is in, and its context: a name that matches them is not a violation, a name that contradicts them (or is unrelated to all of them) is. An image shown to sighted users but hidden from assistive technologies or marked decorative (evidence `exposed_to_assistive_technology: false` with `hidden_reason`: aria-hidden, empty alt, role none/presentation, svg or canvas without an image role or name, CSS background image) is a violation when it conveys information that is not available in text on the page (a logo or emblem naming an organisation, a chart or diagram, a map, a photo or picture the user needs to understand or use the content, e.g. a product photo on its product page, an image that a question or instruction refers to or that shows the answer; a rating, level, status, required-field or warning symbol; an image of text); it is not a violation when it is decorative or illustrative: a flourish, spacer, background pattern or texture, an icon or picture that only repeats adjacent text, or a photo or illustration that sets a mood or illustrates nearby text (e.g. fireworks beside 'Happy new year!', a stock photo beside an article) even if it shows details the text does not mention: such an image is pure decoration under WCAG 1.1.1, and hiding it is correct. Text made of characters chosen for their shape (evidence `lookalike_characters`: a word whose letters come from different alphabets, e.g. a Cyrillic 'Р' or a Greek 'ο' among Latin letters) is non-text content (WCAG Understanding 1.1.1: characters used for their visual appearance): assistive technologies read the foreign letters, not the word sighted users see; a violation when no text alternative gives the intended word (an aria-label or visually hidden text on the element), not a violation when one does or when the word is genuinely written in a language that uses these letters. A missing alt attribute alone is syntax, not this type. Uncertain: the image content or purpose is not in the evidence.
video-captions-inaccurate: WCAG 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (Understanding: captions convey the dialogue and important sounds). Violation: cue text contradicts, changes the meaning of, or substitutes content in the saved authoritative narration or transcript. Not a violation: punctuation, casing or wording differences that keep the meaning. Missing tracks and WebVTT syntax are syntax, not this type. Uncertain: no authoritative reference is in the evidence.
lang-mismatch: WCAG 3.1.1 Language of Page; ACT rule 'HTML page language subtag matches default language'. Compare the declared primary language with the text that has no language of its own (evidence `text_without_own_lang`: the page text outside elements that carry their own lang attribute, including text alternatives such as alt text and aria-label or aria-labelledby names of elements that inherit the page language; a name's language is that of the element it names, even when the name is taken from an element with another lang). Violation: that text is in another language than the declaration. Not a violation: that text matches the declaration, even if passages with their own lang attribute are in other languages and longer. Missing or invalid lang is syntax, not this type. Uncertain: too little text without its own language to determine its language.
language-of-parts-mismatch: WCAG 3.1.2 Language of Parts; ACT rule 'HTML element language subtag matches language'. The passage text includes text alternatives (alt text, aria-label or aria-labelledby names) of elements inside it that inherit its language; a name's language is that of the element it names. Violation: the passage's declared language differs from the language of its text. Exceptions in 3.1.2 are not violations: proper names, technical terms, words of indeterminate language, and words that have become part of the surrounding language. Uncertain: the passage is too short or ambiguous to tell its language.
link-text-mismatch: WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context); ACT rule 'Link in context is descriptive'. The purpose of a link must be determinable from its accessible name together with its programmatically determined context (evidence `context.programmatic_context`): the enclosing sentence or paragraph, list item (in a nested list, also the parent list item under which the list is nested, `parent_list_items`; WCAG technique H81), or table cell with its associated header cells, or text referenced by aria-describedby. Text that is only nearby (a section heading, a neighbouring cell or block that is not associated with the link) is not programmatically determined context (WCAG failure F63). Violation: (a) the name, with that context, states a destination or purpose that the saved destination evidence (destination title, headings, change record, same-page target, or `peeked_destination_v1`: the page the link's URL loads) contradicts; (b) neither the name nor its programmatically determined context identifies where the link goes or what it does, for example 'Download', 'Go', 'Click here', 'Read more' or 'Details' whose context does not name the item, or a name that is a file name, code or URL fragment; a name made only of symbols, icon-font glyphs or private-use characters, which assistive technologies cannot announce meaningfully, whatever the context; a name set by aria-label or aria-labelledby that replaces the link's visible text with a generic phrase (e.g. aria-label 'View link' on a link that shows 'Sell'): the visible text inside the link is then neither its name nor programmatically determined context, so assistive technology users get only the generic phrase; a generic name whose programmatically determined context names only the section or group it belongs to (e.g. a menu heading) but not this link's own destination or action; (c) links with the same name (evidence `links_with_the_same_name`) whose programmatically determined contexts do not tell them apart and which lead to destinations with different purposes or different main content (e.g. one opens a chat page and the other a phone page; compare the link's own destination with each entry's `peeked_destination`); (d) a link hidden from assistive technologies (aria-hidden) that keyboard users can still focus (evidence `hidden_from_assistive_technology: true` and `keyboard_focusable: true`): screen-reader users reach it with no name or purpose; a violation unless it is removed from the focus order. Destinations that are not evidence of a different purpose: an error or placeholder page (an HTTP error, 'not found', a parked or example domain) or the site's generic entry page (its home or index page) shows that a link is broken or unspecific, not that its name misleads; judge such a link by its name and programmatically determined context, except that an in-page link (a skip link or a link to a fragment of the same page) that leaves the page or lands elsewhere is a violation, and a link named as the home page is correct when it leads to the site's entry page. When the destination could not be loaded, its URL (path, file name, query) is evidence of its purpose: a path naming a different topic than the link (e.g. 'Shipping information' linking to /returns-and-refunds) contradicts the name. Not a violation: the destination is described in other words; generic text resolved by its programmatically determined context; links with the same name that lead to the same or an equivalent resource (the same main content in the same form, even if navigation, breadcrumbs or other page furniture differ; different formats or versions of one item, e.g. a web page and a download of it, are different destinations that users choose between); the exception for links whose purpose would be ambiguous to users in general. Uncertain: only when the evidence does not show the name or its programmatically determined context.
button-label-mismatch: WCAG 2.4.6 Headings and Labels and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (the accessible name conveys the control's function). Violation: the name states an action, item or target that the observed result contradicts (for example 'Save' that discards, 'Next' that goes back, or a name for one item when another item is acted on). Judge the result from the recorded changes (field values, evidence `form_value_changes`: fields changed and fields that kept a value; selected options, list order, items shown or removed), not from the application's own status message: a message claiming the named result while the recorded changes show otherwise is a violation (e.g. 'Reset filters' that clears only the search box, 'Newest first' that orders by rating). Not a violation: the result is described in other words or is a plausible part of the named action. Without result evidence: judge the name against the item, section or form the button belongs to; a name for something unrelated to that context is a violation. Uncertain: neither a result nor the context decides.
form-label-mismatch: WCAG 2.4.6 Headings and Labels (Understanding: labels describe the purpose of the field); ACT rule 'Form field label is descriptive'. Violation: the label names a different purpose than the field collects, as shown by its type, name, autocomplete, format hints, validation or the state the form is in; a generic label that names no purpose at all ('Field 1', 'Input', 'Text', 'Value', 'Box'), even if what the field collects is not otherwise grounded. Not a violation: a brief but accurate label; an unchanged label that still fits the field after a transition. Missing labels are syntax, not this type. Uncertain: the field's purpose is not grounded.
widget-label-purpose-mismatch: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value and 2.4.6 Headings and Labels: a tab, menu item, disclosure, option or custom control's name conveys what it selects, opens or controls. Violation: the controlled, revealed or selected content contradicts the name. Judge the result from the recorded changes (field values, evidence `form_value_changes`: fields changed and fields that kept a value; selected options, list order, items shown or removed), not from the application's own status message: a message claiming the named result while the recorded changes show otherwise is a violation (e.g. 'Reset filters' that clears only the search box, 'Newest first' that orders by rating). Not a violation: the content is described in other words. Role or ARIA syntax problems are not this type. Without the controlled content: judge the name against the widget's group and context; a name unrelated to that context is a violation. Uncertain: neither the controlled content nor the context decides.
heading-not-descriptive: WCAG 2.4.6 Headings and Labels; ACT rule 'Heading is descriptive': a heading describes the topic or purpose of the content of its section. Violation: the heading names a different topic, step, item or record than its section content shows, including a heading left from a previous state or naming an item other than the one acted on; a generic heading ('Section', 'Heading', 'Title', 'Content', 'Information', 'More') when its section has its own topic. Not a violation: short, broad or repeated headings that are still accurate; an unchanged heading that still describes the changed content. Headings exposed to assistive technologies but placed off-screen (e.g. role="heading" moved out of view) are headings too and are judged against the content that follows them. Uncertain: the section content is not captured.
landmark-purpose-mismatch: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 1.3.6 Identify Purpose, with the ARIA landmark naming practice: a landmark's role and name describe the purpose of the region. Violation: the name states a purpose that the region's content contradicts, including a name left from a previous state. Not a violation: an unnamed landmark, or a broad but accurate name. Landmark count or nesting is structure, not this type. Uncertain: the region's boundaries or content are not grounded.
page-title-not-descriptive: WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled; ACT rule 'HTML page title is descriptive': the title describes the topic or purpose of the page, which in a single-page application is the current view. Violation: the title names a different page, step, item or view than the current state shows, including a title left from the previous view; a title that names only the site or organisation, or a generic placeholder, when the page has its own specific topic or purpose (e.g. search results, an article, a form). Not a violation: a site name plus an accurate topic; a home page titled with the site name; a title that need not change because the view's purpose did not change. Uncertain: the purpose of the current state cannot be established.
autocomplete-purpose-mismatch: WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose: the autocomplete token must match the purpose of the field. Violation: the token denotes a different purpose than the field collects (for example 'email' on a telephone field); address-type and section tokens are part of the purpose, so 'billing' on a field of the shipping address (or 'shipping' on a billing field) is a mismatch. Not a violation: the token matches the field's purpose. Invalid token syntax is not this type. Uncertain: the field's purpose or the token's purpose is unclear.
aria-state-mismatch: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (states and values can be programmatically determined and match the user interface). Violation: a declared state such as aria-expanded, aria-selected, aria-checked, aria-pressed or aria-current contradicts the rendered or resulting state. Not a violation: the declared state matches what is shown. Invalid ARIA syntax is not this type. Uncertain: the rendered state is not observable in the evidence.
table-header-association-mismatch: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: header associations convey the same relationships as the visual table. Violation: a data cell is associated with a header that does not describe it, so its meaning is misstated. Not a violation: associations that match the row and column meaning. Broken or missing references are syntax, not this type. Uncertain: the table's relationships are not sufficiently captured.
error-message-mismatch: WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification; ACT rule 'Error message describes invalid form field value': when an input error is shown, the item in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text. Violation: (a) the message describes a different field or a different problem than the saved value or validation state shows; (b) the message does not describe the error, e.g. only 'error', 'invalid' or 'please fill the field correctly'; (c) the message does not identify which field is in error when the form has several fields (evidence `page_error_texts` with `referenced_by_a_field: false` and a text that names no field); (d) the only error text is hidden from assistive technologies (`hidden_from_assistive_technology: true`); (e) a field marked invalid whose error is described only by an icon or by a label that does not describe the error (e.g. 'Invalid input', 'error_outline', or a description naming a different problem; evidence `announced_description`); (f) an error summary or alert (evidence `page_error_texts` with the fields in scope) that does not match the fields: it lists an error for a field that is not in error or cannot be changed (disabled, read-only), describes a different problem than a field shows, states a wrong number of errors, or omits fields marked invalid; (g) the message does not identify the field unambiguously, e.g. 'Please fill Name' when several fields share that label (Shipping and Billing); (h) a field shown in error only visually (evidence `visual_error_signals`: an error or flag class, a warning icon, a red border, as the screenshot confirms) with no text that identifies the field and describes the error (WCAG failure F81); not a violation when the visual cue only marks a required field or a focused field and no error is shown; (i) the message names one field but is shown with, or programmatically tied to, a different field (e.g. a message about Diastolic placed under the Systolic field, which is the one marked in error); (j) an error message referenced by a field or its submit control but not shown (evidence `hidden_error_messages` with the form's `form_values`) while a filled-in value fails the requirement it states (e.g. 'Age must be at least 1' hidden while Age holds 0): the error exists but is never shown; not a violation when every filled-in value meets the stated requirements, and an empty field is not in error before the user submits; (k) a field in error whose only error cue is an icon, colour or border while the only text is a hint or instruction that was there before the error (help text stating a range or format): the hint does not identify that an error occurred (F81). Not a violation: the message identifies the field (by its position next to that single field, by naming it, or by an aria-describedby/aria-errormessage reference) and says what is wrong or how to fix it; a message that states a requirement (format, range, required, allowed characters) which the field's current value does not meet is a correct error message: that is exactly the error being described, never a mismatch; a sign-in error such as 'incorrect password' with the field cleared for security. A generic summary such as 'Please correct the errors below' is not a violation when every field in error has its own message. Uncertain: the evidence does not show the message or the field it concerns.
